short: h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp is a new file of PR 4956 (tron pull request 4956, the first of four PRs that split PR 4424). With the build option TRON_K_VNNI on, the PR stores the K cache (the saved keys of attention) of 128-dimension heads in the VNNI layout, the pair-interleaved value order that the AMX tile multiply reads as its B operand. The file defines the typed K plane (the keys of one KV head for one 64-token page) as an owner (k_vnni_tensor) and a view (k_vnni_view), the index map and its constants, the transfer rows, and the operations that move one token's row in and out (store_row, load_row, copy_token).

No raw plane pointer leaves the file except through detail::k_vnni_access, which only the typed operations, the AVX-512 score reader k_vnni::qk_group and the test-only fill may use. The file holds no AMX instruction, no 16-token block operation and no page state: those parts of PR 4424 land in PR 4957, PR 4958 and PR 4959.

This page draws the plane geometry, the hierarchy from a page down to one pair, the type model, the function model, one token's row through the operations and the callers once (section 1), then shows each of the seven logical parts of the file (K0 to K6) beside its diagram (section 2).
base_intro: Six diagrams carry the context that every part below refers to. B1 is the plane geometry and the index map, B1A the hierarchy travel from the K of one page down to one pair, B2 the type model, B3 the function model, B4 the bytes of one token's row through the operations of one forward pass, and B5 the interaction model (which thread calls what). The per-part diagrams in section 2 reuse their shapes and colours and say which base diagram they update.
changes_intro: The file is new, so every line is added. A unit is one logical part: the header comment, the constants with their static_asserts and the index map, the layout gate, the owner and views with the one access route, the transfer rows, the internal address helpers, and one token's row operations. Each unit shows the head code with its comments and, beside it, the diagram that updates a base diagram. Units are ordered as the file is.
trivial_intro: The include lines need no picture.
method: Facts in the diagrams come from the file's own comments (the header comment at head lines 2-37 and the function comments), from Note [K VNNI storage] in kv_cache.hpp (head lines 685-747), and from the callers' code in kv_cache.hpp, model.hpp, self_attention.hpp, full.hpp, gof.hpp, gof.cpp, kernels/k_vnni.hpp and the tests of the same PR. Every line number was read from the PR 4956 head (a5697f86d3) in the worktree, and check_page.py verifies that each cited range contains the box's name.
The worked example (token 37, dimension 70; block 2 of the plane of storage slot 5, KV head 0, page 7; one scoring visit with offsets 0..40 live) is an illustration, not a measurement.

Every figure is an SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics, the drawing format of the figures). Each SVG was rendered to a PNG image (a pixel image) with cairosvg (a Python SVG renderer) and inspected for overlaps and clipped text before delivery.
glossary: AMX

Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. Its tile multiply TDPBF16PS reads its B operand (the second matrix) in the VNNI layout. PR 4956 adds no AMX instruction; the VNNI AMX kernel lands in PR 4957. [k_vnni.hpp:10-17]
AVX-512

Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. One register holds 16 lanes of 32 bits. VDPBF16PS is its instruction that multiplies bf16 pairs and adds the products into fp32 lanes. The reader k_vnni::qk_group and the row operations of this file are AVX-512 code. [k_vnni.hpp:11-12, 16-17]
apply_page_tok

The per-page scoring function of self_attention.hpp. For a VNNI slot it marks every relevant token of the page in the live mask and then calls k_vnni::qk_group once on the read-only view page::k_packed. For a row-major slot it runs the dotter loop over page::k. [self_attention.hpp:1834, 1909, 1953-1954, 1963-1971]
attention workers
The threads that run the attention kernels of a layer, including apply_page_tok. They only read the K plane. [self_attention.hpp:1834]
bf16
The 16-bit brain floating-point format. A bf16 shifted up by 16 bits is the exact fp32 (32-bit float). One 128-dimension K row is 128 bf16 = 256 bytes. [k_vnni.hpp:12, 74-75]
book
The unit of memory allocation of the KV cache. It owns n_pages pages and creates the kv_blocks of every page in one DMA allocation. [kv_cache.hpp:969, 1421, 1448]
book::fill_random / fill_storage_slot

A test-only fill of every kv_block with random bf16 values. fill_storage_slot is its body. It is the one documented exception to the typed packed-K access rule: it reaches a packed plane through detail::k_vnni_access and interprets no coordinates. [kv_cache.hpp:1342, 1767, 1772-1773; k_vnni.hpp:35-37]
copy_storage_slot (page::copy_storage_slot)

Copies count tokens of one storage slot from another page. For a VNNI slot a whole page copies as one owner assignment (dst_block.k = src_block.k) and any other range goes token by token through copy_token, because a token's column depends on its offset in the page. [kv_cache.hpp:2325-2344; 733-736]
copy_token
Copies one token between packed K planes, or within one plane: load_row into a 64-byte-aligned local row, then store_row. The token indices are checked by load_row and store_row. [k_vnni.hpp:286-297]
dense AMX page path

The AMX fast path of software attention for one (query, page) pair: a full 64-token page wholly visible to the query takes the kernel qk_rowmajor_128x4, which reads row-major K. PR 4956 does not compile it for a VNNI slot. [self_attention.hpp:1884-1898; kv_cache.hpp:718-720]
dimension pair (dp) / dword / lane
Dimensions 2 dp and 2 dp + 1 of one token, stored together in one 32-bit lane (a dword, DWORD_BYTES_4). A 512-bit register has 16 such lanes, one per token of a token block. [k_vnni.hpp:13-15, 58-60]
dimension step (s)
32 dimensions = 16 dimension pairs (STEP_DIMS_32, STEP_PAIRS_16): the depth of one AMX tile multiply. HEAD_SIZE_128 / STEP_DIMS_32 = DIM_STEPS_4 steps per head. [k_vnni.hpp:65-67]
DMA

Direct memory access: the transfer engine that moves the staging buffer to the FPGA card. The cache's DMA allocation creates the kv_block objects, so kv_block::k must be trivially constructible (Note [KV block lifetime]). [kv_cache.hpp:1559, 2569-2572; k_vnni.hpp:155-157]
dotter (row-major dotter)

dotter<scalar, 128> in h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp, driven by the per-token dot-product loop of apply_page_tok for a row-major slot. The reader k_vnni::qk_group replaces it for a VNNI slot. [self_attention.hpp:1916-1926, 1956-1960]
FPGA
Field-programmable gate array, the card that runs hardware attention.
GOF / staging

A group of four consecutive tokens. The staging (gof::populate) copies their K/V rows into a buffer that DMA moves to the FPGA card. For a VNNI slot the callback page_info::k_head_fn gathers one row into caller-owned scratch with get_k_row. Idle attention workers run the staging through help_drain_gof and main runs the rest through wait_for_coop_gof. [gof.cpp:186, 201-211; full.hpp:2747-2760; model.hpp:1164-1166, 3231, 3244]
head size
The number of dimensions of one attention head. The VNNI K layout exists for 128-dimension heads only (HEAD_SIZE_128). [k_vnni.hpp:17-18, 57, 86-95]
K row / transfer row (const_k_row_view, k_row_view)

A rank-1 (one-dimensional) typed view of one token's Cols bf16 values in dimension order, carrying the caller's Aligned and Dma flags (defaults true, false). Not packed storage. Built by k_source_row and k_destination_row. [k_vnni.hpp:197-224]
k_at / k_view / page::k

The row-major K views: kv_block::k_view() is the plane as a [token][element] view, k_at(i_page) is one token's row, and page::k returns them for a slot and KV head. They exist for row-major slots only (requires !layout_on). [kv_cache.hpp:1974-2038, 2590-2610]
k_packed (page::k_packed)
The read-only typed view (k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128>) of one page's K plane for a slot and KV head, VNNI slots only. The score reader k_vnni::qk_group reads it. [kv_cache.hpp:2041-2051]
k_source_row / k_destination_row

The builders of the transfer rows. k_source_row makes a read-only row from a const bf16* or from a stride-1 bf16 view that keeps its own flags; k_destination_row makes a writable row from a bf16*. They neither check alignment nor copy. [k_vnni.hpp:206-224]
k_storage / native_k_storage (kv_block::k)
The type of kv_block::k: k_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size> for a VNNI slot, else native_k_storage = bf16[page_size * head_size]. Both hold the same bytes. [kv_cache.hpp:2562-2575]
k_vnni_access (detail::k_vnni_access::plane)

A friend helper with one static function, plane(view), that returns the view's raw pointer to the plane. It is the one route from a view to the address, for the typed operations of this file, k_vnni::qk_group and book::fill_random. [k_vnni.hpp:110-114, 187-195; kv_cache.hpp:701-703]
k_vnni_tensor / k_vnni_view

k_vnni_tensor<64, 128>: the owner of one packed K plane, one 64-byte-aligned bf16 array with no separate allocation. k_vnni_view<T, 64, 128>: the matrix view that knows the address formula; T = bf16 is writable, T = const bf16 read-only. Views come only from the owner's as_view(). [k_vnni.hpp:119-185]
kill switch (TRON_AMX_DISABLE)
The environment variable that turns the AMX kernels off at run time. It keeps the K layout: a TRON_K_VNNI binary then runs the AVX-512 VNNI reader, not the row-major dotter. [kv_cache.hpp:740-746]
KV head / kv_mul

One key/value head of grouped-query attention. One kv_block is the KV cache for one KV head in one KV slot. kv_mul is the number of query heads that share one KV head. [kv_cache.hpp:2559; kernels/k_vnni.hpp:20-21]
kv_block (detail::kv_block)
The KV cache for one KV head in one KV slot of one page: one K plane (k) and one V plane (v). PR 4956 changes the type of k to k_storage. [kv_cache.hpp:2559-2611]
layout_on (k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>)

The layout gate: a constexpr bool that is true only when TRON_K_VNNI is defined and head_size == HEAD_SIZE_128. It depends on the head size only, so every reader and writer of a slot sees the same layout. [k_vnni.hpp:86-95]
live mask (live)

A 64-bit word of apply_page_tok with one bit per token of the page: the tokens the loop found relevant for the query. k_vnni::qk_group scores only those tokens and never reads the K storage of a token whose bit is clear. [self_attention.hpp:1927, 1953-1954; kernels/k_vnni.hpp:23-27]
load_row
Loads one token's K row out of a packed plane: 4 gathers of 16 dwords, one per dimension step, into a transfer row written with unaligned stores. The inverse of store_row. [k_vnni.hpp:269-284]
Note [K VNNI storage]

The kv_cache.hpp note that says who writes and who reads the VNNI K layout: the typed owner and views, the one access route, and the six consumers of a VNNI slot with how each one changes. [kv_cache.hpp:685-747]
Note [KV block lifetime]

The kv_cache.hpp note on how the DMA allocation creates the kv_block objects. It requires kv_block::k to be trivially default constructible, copyable and destructible, which the static_assert at 2569-2572 checks. [kv_cache.hpp:1559]
page (KV page)
The unit of KV storage: 64 contiguous tokens (PAGE_TOKENS_64). The attention computation proceeds page by page. [kv_cache.hpp:1880; k_vnni.hpp:17-18, 56]
page offset (i_page, offset)
A token's position inside its 64-token page, 0..63. Its block is offset / 16 and its lane is offset % 16. [k_vnni.hpp:27-28, 100-102]
pair row

One 64-byte line of a panel: one dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens, 32 bf16 = 16 dwords (ROW_ELEMS_32, ROW_DWORDS_16). The 16 pair rows of a panel are 64 bytes apart (pair_row_offsets). [k_vnni.hpp:14-15, 61-63, 68-69, 240-248]
pair_base / pair_row_offsets

The internal address helpers (namespace k_vnni::detail). pair_base gives the byte address of dimension pair 0 of step s for a token; pair_row_offsets gives the 16 dword offsets of a panel's pair rows, the index vector of the scatter and the gather. [k_vnni.hpp:226-249]
panel

One (s, c) pair of the plane: 16 dimension-pair rows of 64 bytes = 1 KiB (PANEL_BYTES_1024). A panel is exactly one AMX B tile. A plane has N_PANELS_16 = 4 steps x 4 blocks panels, index 4 s + c. [k_vnni.hpp:26-27, 70-73]
plane

K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, the same bytes as the row-major plane. kv_block::k is the plane's owner (k_vnni_tensor) for a VNNI slot. [k_vnni.hpp:18-25; kv_cache.hpp:697-698]
qk_group (k_vnni::qk_group)

The AVX-512 QK score reader of the VNNI plane (h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp). One 64-byte load supplies one dimension pair of 16 tokens; the query's pair is broadcast and multiplied into one accumulator per query head. It reads the plane through detail::k_vnni_access. [kernels/k_vnni.hpp:23-38, 56]
row-major (native K)
One row of head_size bf16 values per token, indexed [p * head_size + i]. Every head size other than 128, and every build without TRON_K_VNNI, keeps this plane. [kv_cache.hpp:2562-2565]
save_k / save_k_impl

The model function that stores the K rows of one layer for every token job of a batch. For a VNNI slot it calls page::set_k_row with k_source_row(kout) per token and KV head; a non-bf16 activation is converted to a bf16 row first. [model.hpp:3074-3118]
scatter / gather

_mm512_i32scatter_epi32 writes the 16 dwords of one register to base + 16 offsets; _mm512_i32gather_epi32 reads 16 dwords from such addresses. store_row scatters, load_row gathers, 4 times per row. [k_vnni.hpp:262-266, 279-283]
set_k_row / get_k_row (page::set_k_row, page::get_k_row)

The layout-agnostic page accessors that store or load one token's K row. For a VNNI slot they call store_row / load_row on the owner's view; for a row-major slot they memcpy one contiguous row. Uniform-geometry overloads forward to them. [kv_cache.hpp:2053-2107]
slot (kv_slot_id, storage slot)

kv_slot_id selects persistent KV storage described by kv_slot_specs (a geometry and a retention policy). A VNNI slot is a slot whose geometry has 128-dimension heads in a TRON_K_VNNI build. [kv_cache.hpp:687-692]
store_row

Stores one token's K row into a packed plane: 4 scatters of 16 dwords, one per dimension step, into the token's column of its block's 4 panels. Only this token's 64 pair slots are written. [k_vnni.hpp:251-267]
token block (c)

16 consecutive tokens of a page (BLOCK_TOKENS_16), page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15. A page has TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 blocks. The block's bytes are its 4 panels, one per dimension step. [k_vnni.hpp:22-27, 63-64]
tron
The inference program under test (the project's CLAUDE.md term list). Every type of this header is declared inside namespace tron. [k_vnni.hpp:52]
TRON(this_lifetimebound)
The attribute macro for __attribute__((lifetimebound)) on this: the compiler warns when a returned view outlives the object it came from. [h/common/attributes.hpp:663-674; k_vnni.hpp:164, 170]
TRON_K_VNNI

A CMake option (default OFF). When defined, layout_on<128> is true and the K plane of every 128-dimension head holds the VNNI layout. The definition is PUBLIC so every translation unit that touches a KV page sees the same layout. [CMakeLists.txt:47; src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:226-234; k_vnni.hpp:89-91]
VNNI

Vector Neural Network Instructions layout. The two values of a dimension pair of one token sit next to each other in one 32-bit lane; one 64-byte row holds that pair for 16 consecutive tokens. It is the B-operand layout of the AMX tile multiply and the operand layout of VDPBF16PS. [k_vnni.hpp:12-17]

base.title: Data model: one K plane, its panels, pair rows and the index map
base.intro: A plane is K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, the same bytes as the row-major plane. It is 16 panels of 1 KiB, indexed by dimension step s and token block c. A panel is 16 pair rows of 64 bytes. A pair row holds one dimension pair of 16 tokens. Every arrow says how many. The worked example (token 37, dimension 70) is traced through the index formula.

base.title: The hierarchy travel: the K of one page -> plane -> token block and dimension step -> panel -> pair row -> pair
base.intro: One chain of carve-outs, each level drawn from the one above: the K of one KV page for one storage slot is one plane per KV head; a plane is the 64 x 128 grid; a dimension step cuts its columns and a token block cuts its rows, so a panel is one cell of the 4 x 4 cut; inside a panel the 32 dimensions are 16 pairs; the VNNI form stores the panel as 16 pair rows; a dword of a pair row is one pair of one token. The worked example (token 37, dimension 70) is followed down every level and through the index formula. B1 above stays as the reference drawing.

base.title: Type model: owner, views, the one access route, and the transfer rows
base.intro: k_vnni_tensor owns the bytes. k_vnni_view is the only way to name a plane, and detail::k_vnni_access::plane the only way to get its address. The transfer rows const_k_row_view / k_row_view carry one token's 128 values in dimension order. The diagram shows what each type can and cannot do and who is a friend of whom.

base.title: Function model: every operation of the file, its callers and callees
base.intro: The operations are grouped by purpose: index map and gate, views, transfer rows, the internal address helpers, and one token's row. Every cell says in one line what the function does and cites its definition. Callers in other files of the PR sit at the left.

base.title: Sequencing model: the bytes of one token's row through the operations
base.intro: Block 2 of the worked example (the plane of slot 5, KV head 0, page 7) passes through store_row (save_k), the masked read of k_vnni::qk_group (one scoring visit), load_row (the FPGA staging) and copy_token (a page copy). The diagram shows which operation touches which bytes of the block's 4 KiB. The grey columns are the tokens whose row is not saved yet: no operation reads or writes them.

base.title: Interaction model: who calls which operation from which thread
base.intro: The operations of this file are called from kv_cache.hpp (page accessors), model.hpp (save_k), self_attention.hpp (attention workers), full.hpp and gof.cpp (the FPGA staging), and the page copies. Lanes are kinds of threads or callers. The rules under the lanes cite the comment that states each one.

units.title: The header comment: what the file defines, the plane layout formula, who may compute a packed address
lead: Comment text only. The four paragraphs name the file's contents, the Words used here, the index formula of the plane, and the rule that only the typed operations and the score reader k_vnni::qk_group compute a packed address [k_vnni.hpp:2-37].
The plane formula: plane[(((s * 4 + c) * 16 + dp) * 16 + t) * 2 + j] == K[c * 16 + t][s * 32 + 2 * dp + j]. One (s, c) is one 1 KiB panel, exactly one AMX B tile [k_vnni.hpp:21-27].
Token i owns column (i % 16) of token block (i / 16) in every panel. So tokens are written independently, with no read-modify-write between tokens [k_vnni.hpp:27-29].

Cache code, the model, hardware staging and the tests use the typed operations or the page accessors built on them (page::set_k_row, page::get_k_row, page::k_packed). book::fill_random is the one documented exception [k_vnni.hpp:31-37].

units.title: The layout constants, their static_asserts and the index map
lead: Every constant names its value. A page has PAGE_TOKENS_64 tokens in TOKEN_BLOCKS_4 blocks of BLOCK_TOKENS_16. A head has HEAD_SIZE_128 dimensions in DIM_STEPS_4 steps of STEP_DIMS_32 = STEP_PAIRS_16 pairs. A pair row is one LINE_BYTES_64 line = ROW_ELEMS_32 bf16 = ROW_DWORDS_16 dwords. A panel is PANEL_ELEMS_512 bf16 = PANEL_BYTES_1024 = PANEL_DWORDS_256 dwords. A plane has N_PANELS_16 panels [k_vnni.hpp:56-73].
Six constants are literal definitions (PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128, PAIR_2, DWORD_BYTES_4, LINE_BYTES_64, STEP_DIMS_32). Every other constant is derived from them [k_vnni.hpp:56-73].

BF16_BITS_16 and HIGH_HALF_0XFFFF0000 have no reader in this file. They serve the float-query path of k_vnni::qk_group, which widens the stored bf16 pairs to fp32 with a shift or a mask [k_vnni.hpp:74-77; kernels/k_vnni.hpp:79-82].

The static_assert at lines 78-82 pins the 10 derived constants to the number in their names. The static_assert at lines 83-84 states that the VNNI plane has the same element count as the row-major plane [k_vnni.hpp:78-84].

index(token, dim) computes the element index of K[token][dim] from (s, c, dp, t, j) as the header formula says [k_vnni.hpp:97-106]. Its production reader is k_vnni_view::at [k_vnni.hpp:139]. The layout test pins it with compile-time anchors and checks that the bytes store_row writes agree with it [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:90-104, 131, 164, 183].

units.title: The layout gate layout_on and who branches on it
lead: layout_on<head_size> is true only for HEAD_SIZE_128 heads and only when TRON_K_VNNI is defined. Otherwise it is false for every head size [k_vnni.hpp:89-95].
The gate depends on the head size only, not on the query type or on AMX availability. So every reader and writer of a slot sees the same layout [k_vnni.hpp:86-88]. Its consumers, one per bullet:
kv_block::k_storage picks k_vnni_tensor or the bf16 array [kv_cache.hpp:2566-2568].
The row views page::k, kv_block::k_view and k_at exist only for row-major slots, and page::k_packed only for VNNI slots [kv_cache.hpp:1978-2033, 2044-2045, 2593-2610].
set_k_row, get_k_row, copy_storage_slot and fill_storage_slot branch on it with if constexpr [kv_cache.hpp:2062, 2079, 2331, 1772].
In model.hpp, save_k_impl stores a row with set_k_row for a VNNI slot and through page::k otherwise [model.hpp:3100-3115].

In self_attention.hpp, the dense AMX page path is not compiled for a VNNI slot, and apply_page_tok collects a live mask and calls k_vnni::qk_group instead of the dotter loop [self_attention.hpp:1884-1886, 1909-1971].

In full.hpp, the FPGA staging callback page_info::k_head_fn gathers the row with get_k_row for a VNNI slot [full.hpp:2751-2756]. The tests check the gate and both sides [t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:165-168; t_llama_unit.cpp:1098-1101; t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:356-360].

units.title: The typed owner, its views and the one access route
lead: k_vnni_view<T, 64, 128> (T = bf16 or const bf16, concept k_vnni_element) is a matrix view with a bounds-checked at(token, dim) and no element write. There is no public pointer access: a bare pointer does not say which layout it points at [k_vnni.hpp:116-153].

A writable view (bf16) converts to a read-only one (const bf16), never the reverse [k_vnni.hpp:129-133]. Only three friends reach the private members: k_vnni_tensor, detail::k_vnni_access and the other instantiations of k_vnni_view [k_vnni.hpp:143-146].

k_vnni_tensor<64, 128> owns the 16 KiB plane as one 64-byte-aligned bf16 array, with no initialization: the cache's DMA allocation creates the kv_blocks that hold it [k_vnni.hpp:155-180; kv_cache.hpp:1559]. kv_block::k is this type for a VNNI slot [kv_cache.hpp:2566-2568].

as_view() on a named owner returns a writable view for a non-const owner and a read-only view for a const owner, both marked TRON(this_lifetimebound). as_view() on a temporary is deleted [k_vnni.hpp:163-176]. The static_assert pins sizeof to 16 KiB and alignof to 64 bytes [k_vnni.hpp:181-185].

detail::k_vnni_access::plane(view) is the only route from a view to the plane address. Its users are the typed operations of this file, the score reader k_vnni::qk_group and the test-only book::fill_random [k_vnni.hpp:110-114, 187-195; kv_cache.hpp:701-703; kernels/k_vnni.hpp:56; kv_cache.hpp:1773].

units.title: Transfer rows: const_k_row_view, k_row_view and their builders
lead: A transfer row (const_k_row_view / k_row_view) is one token's Cols bf16 values in dimension order with the caller's Aligned and Dma flags. It is not packed storage [k_vnni.hpp:197-204].

Aligned is not a precondition: store_row and load_row use unaligned loads and stores, unlike the packed V rows [k_vnni.hpp:198-199]. The flag defaults are the bare literals true and false [k_vnni.hpp:200, 203, 206, 220].

k_source_row builds a read-only row from a bf16 pointer, or from a rank-1 bf16 view with Stride == 1 that keeps its own flags. k_destination_row builds a writable row from a pointer. The builders neither check alignment nor copy data [k_vnni.hpp:206-224].
Consumers, one per bullet:
save_k_impl passes k_source_row(kout) for a bf16 K buffer row, and k_source_row<head_size>(row) for a row converted to bf16 on the stack through k_destination_row [model.hpp:3104-3111].
page_info::k_head_fn passes k_destination_row<head_size>(dest) to get_k_row for the FPGA staging [full.hpp:2754-2755].

page::set_k_row and get_k_row take the row with the caller's Aligned and Dma flags [kv_cache.hpp:2054-2060, 2071-2077]. In this header, copy_token builds its local row with both helpers [k_vnni.hpp:295-296].

units.title: Address arithmetic: pair_base and pair_row_offsets
lead: pair_base gives the byte address of dimension pair 0 of step s for a token: panel (s, c) plus the token's column t (i % 16). It has two overloads, bf16* and const bf16* [k_vnni.hpp:227-239]. store_row and load_row call it DIM_STEPS_4 = 4 times per row, once per step [k_vnni.hpp:264, 281].

pair_row_offsets lists the 16 pair rows of a panel, 64 bytes = 16 dwords apart, as the index vector of the scatter and the gather [k_vnni.hpp:240-248]. store_row and load_row call it once per row [k_vnni.hpp:261, 278].
Both helpers live in namespace k_vnni::detail and have no caller outside this file [k_vnni.hpp:226, 249].

units.title: One token's row into and out of the packed plane: store_row, load_row, copy_token
lead: store_row scatters one token's 128-dimension row: 4 scatters of 16 dwords, one per dimension step, into the token's column of its block's 4 panels. Only this token's 64 pair slots are written [k_vnni.hpp:251-267].
load_row is the inverse: 4 gathers of 16 dwords into a row written with unaligned stores [k_vnni.hpp:269-284].

Callers: page::set_k_row and get_k_row call store_row and load_row for a VNNI slot and memcpy one contiguous row otherwise [kv_cache.hpp:2062-2067, 2079-2084]. The tests call them directly [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:77, 124, 148; t_phase1_integration.cpp:869].

copy_token moves one token between planes through a 64-byte-aligned local row: load_row, then store_row. The token indices are checked by those two [k_vnni.hpp:286-297]. copy_storage_slot uses it for every page copy that does not cover a whole page [kv_cache.hpp:2339-2343]. The layout test calls it directly [t_k_vnni_layout.cpp:174].

trivial.title: Includes
trivial.what: The include lines of the header. kv_cache_fwd.hpp (line 48) forward-declares k_vnni_tensor and k_vnni_view so intrinsics-free headers can name them [kv_cache_fwd.hpp:39-48]. view.hpp and seq.hpp (lines 49-50) define the rank-1 view and const_view and seq / sseq that K4's row aliases name [view.hpp:116, 361; seq.hpp]. immintrin.h (line 42) supplies the AVX-512 intrinsics of K5 and K6.
